issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual description indicate acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name: String, ingredient name: String, price: int, quantity: int), but the template/solution usage and implementation use a three-parameter signature (ingredient name: String, price: int, quantity: int). This mismatch in method parameters will confuse students about the required method signature and which parameters to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement and UML consistent with the template/solution by specifying the acceptSupplyDelivery signature as acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Alternatively, update the template and solution to implement the four-parameter signature (including supplier name) everywhere. Ensure examples in Main and tests match the chosen signature.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize both attributes (orders and stock) in the SealSaloon constructor, but it also requires the stock attribute to be static and final (shared across instances). A static final field cannot be properly initialized in an instance constructor. This contradictory instruction (initialize stock in constructor vs. make it static final) is structurally inconsistent and would prevent students from following both requirements.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: either (A) require stock to be a static final field and state that it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor), or (B) make stock an instance final field and allow initialization in the constructor. Update the problem statement and UML to reflect the chosen approach so students can implement a compilable design.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should accept four parameters including a supplier name (signature: acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)), but the provided solution and the commented usage in the template use a three-parameter form (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch (both in parameter count and parameter roles/names) creates confusion about the intended method signature and which information must be handled (the supplier parameter is referenced in the problem but absent in implementation).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the signature across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution and template to implement the four-parameter signature including supplierName (e.g., public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)) and update all call sites, or (B) update the problem statement/UML to specify the three-parameter signature actually used (ingredientName, price, quantity). Prefer option A if supplier information is intended to be part of the exercise.
